title: Fastest Land, Air, And Sea Vehicles In GTA 6 And How To Get Them
summary: From the moment you set foot on the map of Leonida, you likely have a side goal of acquiring the fastest vehicle possible in Grand Theft Auto 6 . It might not be your immediate objective, especially seeing as you're stuck with a single car until Chapter 2, but the thought is always lurking in the back of your mind. Even after you get the ability to own and register vehicles, though, you still have little to no idea which vehicles are actually the fastest in GTA 6. Whether you're searching for a car, motorcycle, boat, or plane, there's no way to know what's the fastest until you WAiNK every vehicle in Leonida. Or, you can look at the guide below to see the fastest vehicle of every kind in GTA 6. In This Article Fastest vehicles in GTA 6 Fastest car in GTA 6 - Truffade Thrax Fastest motorcycle in GTA 6 - Nagasaki SFB 1000 Fastest off-road vehicle in GTA 6 - '72 Cliffhanger Fastest boat in GTA 6 - Speeder 700 GT Fastest aircraft in GTA 6 - Hauners P-996 Lazer Fastest vehicles in GTA 6 We'll be going over the vehicles with the fastest stock speed ratings across all classes in GTA 6. This includes cars, motorcycles, off-road vehicles, boats, and all types of aircraft (planes, choppers, etc.). It's also important to highlight that we're talking about the stock speed ratings for all vehicles, so any upgraded vehicles won't count on this list. For example, Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax is faster than the stock Truffade Thrax, but that's only due to aftermarket parts being installed on the car. To keep things simple, we're listing the fastest vehicles by default in GTA 6. Below, you can see each vehicle class, the fastest vehicle in that class, and where to find the vehicle in GTA 6. Fastest car in GTA 6 - Truffade Thrax Giorgio's Truffade Thrax in Pegassi Tower. We've previously done a deep dive into the top five fastest cars in GTA 6 , but the Truffade Thrax remains the fastest stock car in all of Leonida (8.7 speed rating). Even with other cars, like the Royal Ruby Progen Emerus , having a higher speed rating, that's with fully upgraded parts. A fully upgraded Truffade Thrax remains faster than any other car in the game (9.2 speed rating), and that likely won't change even after players discover every legendary car in GTA 6. To find the Truffade Thrax, you can use a couple of different methods. However, the best way to get your hands on this vehicle is to find Andrew Node's Thrax in a mansion's garage on Starfish Island. You can glitch into the garage or complete the "No Flusher" side objective to gain free entry. Andrew Node's Thrax is free to steal, but costs $70K to register. Fastest motorcycle in GTA 6 - Nagasaki SFB 1000 Jason riding the Nagasaki SFB 1000. Next up, we have motorcycles, and there are a few fantastic choices in this vehicle class if you're looking for pure speed. However, the fastest cycle by stock speed rating in GTA 6 is the Nagasaki SFB 1000 . There are a couple of Principe motorcycles, such as the Burnished Alvino, with a higher speed rating, but those are considered aftermarket vehicles. By default, the Nagasaki SFB 1000 has the best speed rating: 7.1, which even beats out some supercars. To acquire the Nagasaki SFB 1000, you just have to progress Dre'Quan's questline in GTA 6. Eventually, Dre'Quan will tell you to go to a garage in Vice City to pick up a present, and that present is the motorcycle. You'll still have to register it, but there's a sizable discount on the fee. Fastest off-road vehicle in GTA 6 - '72 Cliffhanger The possible spawn point for the '72 Cliffhanger. We're throwing all off-road vehicles into the mix for this entry, but mainly focusing on dirt bikes, four-wheelers, and other vehicles meant to be driven through trails and at the Mud Club . If we ignore converted cars, like the Dominator Buggy, then we're left with the '72 Cliffhanger as the fastest off-road vehicle in GTA 6. With a speed rating of 4.9, you won't find a faster dirt bike anywhere else, even though the classic Sanchez does come close. There's not a guaranteed spawn for the '72 Cliffhanger in GTA 6 yet, but most players have found success looking around the parking lots at the Ocean View Hotel in Ocean Beach, which is on the eastside of Vice City proper. If you don't find the bike there, reload your save and check again until it spawns. You can also find the Magma Cliffhanger variant of the bike near a shack in the northern stretch of land in Watson Bay. Fastest boat in GTA 6 - Speeder 700 GT The cheat section for the Speeder 700 GT. Boats in GTA 6 don't play a major role in any of the story or side content, despite a chunk of Leonida featuring traversable waterways and oceans. So, we don't have a ton of information about all of the boats in the game, but by current accounts, the fastest boat is the Speeder 700 GT . There are no detailed speed stats for the Speeder 700 GT yet, but based on testing, it doesn't appear as though any other boat can match its raw speed. Right now, the only way to get the Speeder 700 GT is by using a cheat code in GTA 6, which doesn't unlock until after the main story ends. The cheat code unlocks after you "complete five combat challenges." Perhaps some guaranteed spawn will be discovered in the future, but none exist as far as we currently know. Fastest aircraft in GTA 6 - Hauners P-996 Lazer The Mile Zero Air Station location. Similar to boats, we simply don't have a wealth of information surrounding aircraft and their speeds in GTA 6. A solid guess for the fastest aircraft, though, is the Hauners P-996 Lazer, which seems to be the lone fighter jet in the game. Having used the Hauners P-996 Lazer ourselves, it would be surprising to see any other plane or chopper surpass its raw speed. The Hauners P-996 Lazer jas a single spawn in GTA 6 , and it's located at the Mile Zero Air Station. You can find the air station in the southwest corner of the map, but you'll have to break in and deal with armored guards, heavy vehicles, and even tanks . There's also a cheat code for the fighter jet, which is unlocked after you "complete all challenges" in GTA 6. And that wraps up the fastest vehicles in GTA 6. We should know more concrete details about the boats and aircraft later down the line, but the actual vehicles in the list likely won't change anytime soon. title: How To Rob Banks In GTA 6
summary: It goes without saying that you’ll commit countless crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6 . From punching hapless civilians and stealing their cars, to threatening storeowners as you take their hard-earned cash, the world is yours for the taking. Now, you’re about to level up as you rob banks all over Leonida. In This Article Requirements before you rob banks in GTA 6 Dye Pack Jammer Snap Gun Yasmani as a fence Classifications of bank jobs in Leonida Tips before you start your break in Suppressors/silencers Alternate entrances Disguises Focus mode: Alarms, cameras, and security Raking in cash and dealing with NPCs How to open safes ATMs and vaults Requirements before you rob banks in GTA 6 Before you run off to any bank, you should first consider some key requirements. These require you to play through the campaign until you reach chapter 3, whereupon you’ll be able to tackle various main missions for two NPCs: Raul and Yasmani. Dye Pack Jammer You receive this permanent upgrade as part of a main mission called Credit Check. Prior to this point, any packets of marked money you obtain may have anti-theft devices that explode. Whenever this occurs, your character will be covered in a bright pink color, making it easier for cops to recognize you. Worse, the marked money will be defaced and ruined, rendering it useless. Snap Gun During chapter 3, you’ll be introduced to Yasmani, who’ll task you with hitting three jewelry stores in Vice City. Do these objectives to receive the Snap Gun, a tool that enables a lockpicking minigame. This lets you open locked doors, which could be used as alternate entrances. Yasmani as a fence Yasmani also becomes a fence NPC. Compared to Tyrone, who pays you a lot for drugs, Yasmani prefers to deal in marked money and jewelry. So, anytime you’ve got marked money on you, be sure to exchange it with him. Note: Yasmani also gives you info on which banks might have a lot more cash than usual, but this info comes at a price. Classifications of bank jobs in Leonida If you want to rob banks in GTA 6, you must take note of the different kinds of jobs. You can find these in the GTA Index - Robberies tab: Bank jobs - This is where you target small and large banks in the city, which have a cash drawer and a safe. Payouts range from as low as $5,000 to as high as $45,000. Big bank jobs - This is where you target companies like Fleeca and Lombank. Not only do these buildings have a cash drawer and a safe, but they also have a vault. If you’re lucky, you could earn $200,000 or more. Tips before you start your break in Suppressors/silencers It goes without saying that you and your partner need to have weapons with suppressors/silencers. Always buy this type of upgrade for your chosen firearms in Ammu-Nation stores. Note: Silenced firearms prevent any noise that might startle security guards, tellers, and customers. Once the alarm is raised and others start shooting, the gunfire will get reported to the police. In just a few seconds, you’ll have cops ruining all the fun. Alternate entrances Don’t just go through the main entrance when you rob banks in GTA 6. Instead, check your surroundings to see if there are alternate passageways. Examples include doors and shutters that you can unlock using the Snap Gun. Likewise, there might be hatches or openings on rooftops. Disguises It’s also a good idea to bring a disguise with you: Masks, bandanas, caps, and eyewear can all be toggled on or off in the Loadout - Items screen. If you get spotted wearing these, then be sure to toggle them off when you escape. Doing so helps clear the appearance heat when the police are searching for you. Ideally, you should have a different set of clothing in your registered vehicle’s trunk. When you make your getaway, you’ll be able to switch to something else quickly. Focus mode: Alarms, cameras, and security The moment you enter a bank, activate focus mode by pressing both thumbsticks simultaneously. This will show outlines even through walls and obstacles, as well as targeting spots. Be careful when kicking doors with a red glow, as doing so triggers the alarm. Use your Snap Gun to stealthily unlock them. Check for any security guards that are milling about in rooms, as well as tellers/staff that might make a run for it. In addition to this, look at the ceiling for any cameras that are recording you and shoot them immediately. Those with a yellow glow have local CCTV footage that can be destroyed via terminals. Those with a red glow have footage saved in the cloud. You can’t do anything about this, which means you do need to change your disguise/outfit later to remove heat. Lastly, if the alarms start blaring, you can disable them by interacting with a device usually mounted on the wall of the security office. Raking in cash and dealing with NPCs You also need to be mindful of NPCs when you rob banks in GTA 6. You do want to amass as much money as possible, but you don’t want a firefight to break out. When you see an NPC, bring out your silenced weapon and decide what to do with them: Threatening an NPC might work just to get them to empty the cash register. However, you need to have your eyes on them at all times. Getting distracted could cause aggressive NPCs to (a) bolt for the exit, (b) press the alarm, or (c) fight back. Incapacitating NPCs is a better idea. You can either do a melee attack (for tellers/staff) or shoot them in the knee (guards). Killing NPCs outright isn’t recommended, as this worsens your criminal profile due to aggressive and cruel behavior. How to open safes Outside of missions where the safe code is already provided to you, there are other ways to learn the combination: Investigate the rooms and look for a note or document that has the code. Activate focus mode and look for the teller/staff that has a yellow glow. Threaten this person to make them divulge the passcode. If you knock out/kill a bunch of NPCs, loot the bodies in case one of them has the code. There’s also one final option where you blow up the safe, though this might impact the amount of money that you’re able to recover. If you’re okay with this, go grab some Sticky Bombs (C4) from Yasmani’s storeroom or from any Ammu-Nation shop. ATMs and vaults Last but not least, robbing banks in the game might also make you curious about other related facets. If you want to steal ATMs , you need to tow them out of the wall. You must also have the means to open them to grab the lockboxes inside. As for cracking open vaults , you’ll be able to do so much later in chapter 4. Yasmani will have a mission for you called That’s Where the Money Is. He’ll also give you tips about armored vans moving around the city, and you can tail them to learn which vaults are being opened at that moment. You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub .

title: How To Open Bank Vaults In GTA 6
summary: From the start of Chapter 4 in Grand Theft Auto 6 , you'll get the opportunity to rob banks in GTA 6 . Previously, you could rob pawn shops, jewelry stores, and other small-time locations. However, after receiving the Dye Pack Jammer from Karim, you can rob big-time banks by stealing all of its marked bills. Robbing a big bank has its challenges, though, and one of the tougher problems they present is breaking into the vault. Every big bank has a vault you can rob in GTA 6, but they can't be opened using traditional methods. If you want the biggest score possible, though, you'll have to learn the one method to break into any bank vault. How to get inside any bank vault in GTA 6 Chances are, if you're reading this guide, you tried to rob a large Fleeca bank only to make it inside and realize the vault door is closed. Unlike the bank's safe, you can't enter a code or use one of your lockpicking tools to open the vault and steal all the cash inside. While there are rare instances where you might find a bank's vault open, they're almost always closed unless you use one specific method in GTA 6. The only way to break into a bank vault is by waiting for an armored security truck driver to open it themselves. You might have seen these trucks driving around the map, but their sole job is to deliver briefcases full of cash inside bank vaults across Vice City. You can get lucky and spot one of these trucks yourself, but the best way to locate them is by going through Yasmani. Yasmani is a fence whom you meet during Chapter 3 through Boobie. At first, Yasmani just looks like another fence who buys illegal goods from you in GTA 6. However, as you progress, it's revealed that Yasmani can offer you tips on potential jobs in exchange for a small fee. Yasmani is a fence in GTA 6, but also offers tips on money-making jobs. The one job you're looking for from Yasmani is a tip about a security truck that is planned to make a stop at a bank vault. This tip costs you $10,000 every time, but it's a repeatable job from Yasmani that you can profit 10x from if you do it right. All you have to do is continue returning to Yasmani after each completed job, and you'll receive another from him. Not every tip is about a security truck, but Yasmani's jobs are always profitable, so they're worth doing regardless. In any case, once you pay the $10,000 for the tip about a security truck, you'll see the truck's purple icon appear on your map. Your job from here is to tail the truck until it makes a stop at a bank. It's important not to commit crimes around the truck, though, as this alerts the driver to you, causing it to speed away. The objective to tail a security truck in GTA 6. Once the truck has parked outside of a bank, wait for the passenger to get out with a briefcase and walk through the front entrance. You now have to follow the passenger inside the bank, preferably without a visible gun on your back, and give them a few seconds to open the vault doors. Of course, the vault isn't visible from the bank lobby, so you either have to sneak past the guards and into the back offices, or rob the bank. The latter option is really only doable with both Jason and Lucia present, but you can sneak around to the vault using just one character. Entering a bank vault full of marked bills. After you find the vault, it should be open, and marked bills will be on a cart in front of the security deposit boxes. Take as many marked bills as you can carry and get out of the bank before the cops show up. You can also open some security deposit boxes along the vault walls if you have time. Now, your job is simply getting back to Yasmani in one piece. With a full haul from a bank vault, you can expect to sell around $80-100K worth of marked bills to Yasmani, who pays the highest amount for them. However, if you also rob the entire bank, including the safe and cashier drawers, you're looking at an extra $25-50K. This is by far the best way to make money in GTA 6 , but it's not something you can always rely on, and you have to wait until Chapter 4 to do it. title: How To Talk To Your Relatives (And Their Cool-Ass Kids) About GTA 6 This Thanksgiving
summary: Every Thanksgiving brings the possibility of fraught conversations. Your sister's divorce. Your second cousin's polycule. Politics . So surely one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, and certainly the biggest one of the year, will come up in conversation. Your relatives might not know much about Grand Theft Auto 6, and as the designated video gamer of the family, all eyes may turn to you to explain what's going on. How do you broach this delicate topic with your loved ones? How do you explain what's so special and momentous about this moment in video games? Do you show them Mandy? (Don't.) In the interest of doing our due diligence and public service, we've compiled a brief guide on how to talk with your family about GTA 6 this Thanksgiving. Somewhere in between the parade and your third slice of pie, your relatives may come away with a better understanding of this cultural moment, and of video games more broadly. Grand Theft Auto 6 What's the big deal, anyway? Grand Theft Auto 6 made nearly $4 billion on its first day of release , and sold an astonishing 32.5 million copies. That's a number that most entertainment properties would love to hit in lifetime sales, and GTA did it in a day . That also puts it on-track to be one of the biggest entertainment launches of all time, rivaling most big-budget movies in lifetime grosses. Analysts have compared it to everything from The Avengers to Taylor Swift. Aside from the financial success, it's also a critical hit. At a 99 Metacritic rating, it has tied for the top-reviewed game of all time . The other contender is the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which got a well-regarded but not as high-scoring remake this year. So GTA 6 is about as close as we're getting to a monoculture in today's fractious media environment. Everybody online is talking about it and responding to it and the discourse is shaping a lot of conversation. So even if you aren't actively playing it, chances are you're going to see clips or reactions or Easter eggs. That goes double if you're a younger person, or if you're interested in video games. Grand Theft Auto 6 So why is this one so big? GTA 6 has been 13 years in the making, and anticipation had been building for all that time. It's a follow-up to the also wildly successful Grand Theft Auto 5, which spent years topping sales charts even after release because people just kept buying it. Expectations for this game were sky-high, and by actually managing to meet those expectations, it's become something of a cultural explosion. Every GTA game is a sprawling open world with tons to do and see, and GTA 6 is larger and more detailed than ever. The fictional setting of Leonida is huge and varied, with lots of different environments that capture both urban and rural settings with incredible detail. This one also took a lot of lessons from Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption 2, which means a slower pace and finer sim-like control over how to react to situations. And then on top of that, Rockstar has built a bunch of emergent events to trigger as you explore, so it's easy to spend tons of time in the world. Fun events will just find you if you wander around, even off the beaten path or away from mission quests. GTA 6 is also getting a lot of praise and attention for its leads, Jason and Lucia. Rockstar had posed this as a Bonnie & Clyde story, and that romantic relationship is really at the heart of the story here. There's a lot more focus given to growing their bonds, and little moments of domestic tranquility like relaxing and watching TV with your partner, or picking up groceries. Grand Theft Auto 6 I heard people are mad that it's "woke." GTA 6 has also been the topic of some backlash, in part because of the relationship between Jason and Lucia. The game spends some time, especially at the beginning, establishing their relationship at a slower pace. Jason learns Lucia is getting released early from prison and spends time fixing up his house and getting ready for her to arrive. That can involve things like picking up flowers, buying her a nice necklace, and getting a haircut. It's all very cute. GTA 6 is also the first game in the series in which you can play as a woman. But exactly because it's a cultural juggernaut, there's money to be made in the attention economy, including rage-bait. Rockstar has made the sim aspects much more detailed than before, but at the same time, it also removed some aspects that were problematic or no longer made sense in the context of these characters--most famously, the ability to solicit (and then assault) sex workers. Generally speaking, GTA 6 is a broad satire of America, and that includes poking fun at lots of different groups, though Rockstar has said it was more cautious this time not to "punch down" at vulnerable people. The satire works best when it's mocking the media and other elites, and there's lots of that here. This is a more thoughtful GTA, but it's still very much GTA. Grand Theft Auto 6 Should I let my child play it? He's six. Only if he's really cool. Okay seriously, this game isn't really meant for kids, and especially not for younger kids. There's a lot of very adult content. Radio stations will detail sexual misconduct allegations against a star football player and then have a commercial for a vibrator. Characters are frequently shown in sexual situations--sometimes as a gag, other times as a sensual love scene. And as a game that's fundamentally about crime, it's all awash in graphic violence. You can mow down pedestrians, kill citizens or police officers, and be cruel to animals and pets. The open-world aspect allows you to do lots of things that are, in the context of the real world, pretty terrible! And that's aside from the story cutscenes, where violence regularly happens to characters, and is presented in higher fidelity than any previous GTA game. You should use your own discretion regarding what your child can handle. However, if you have kids who are of the age where they're hearing about GTA, or their friends are playing GTA or showing them videos, you should definitely talk with them about it, regardless of whether you let them play it. Ask questions about what they're interested in and what kinds of things they've seen. Lots of videos going around are harmless fun, so don't necessarily be alarmed if they say they saw a video of it at school. But do stay on top of what they're seeing, because it could cross your own personal boundaries for your kids. Grand Theft Auto 6 So it's just a violence simulator? The Grand Theft Auto series is an open-world sandbox, which by its nature involves loads of freedom to do whatever you want. A lot of the fun comes from experimenting with the boundaries of the world and seeing how it reacts. So that can involve violence, and the nature of the story often requires you to engage in daring heists, shootouts, and vehicle escapes where collateral damage is hard to avoid. However, the game doesn't really encourage violence, per se. Violent actions are punished by attracting police, and if they catch or kill you, you'll lose the resources you've gathered. If you engage in too much wanton violence your criminal profile will grow more hardened, which will impact your characters. And while the open world is ripe for violence, it's also full of more wholesome activities. You can lose hours just wandering the world, playing pool, going golfing, scuba diving for treasure, and more. Plus you can get rewarded for good deeds, like stopping a mugger or helping a neighbor fix his engine. You can even follow traffic laws. Outside of the story missions, how much violence you engage in is really up to you. Grand Theft Auto 6 What are good alternatives for younger kids? GTA is the biggest open-world sandbox game around, but there have been lots of other games that have attempted similar gameplay, including some that are perfectly kid-friendly. A few favorites are Lego games like Lego City Undercover or Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, both of which take place in large open worlds and have a variety of vehicles to drive around. If you want to cause chaos you could try something like Untitled Goose Game or Goat Simulator, or if you're more interested in the street racing aspect you may want to play a Forza or Mario Kart game. Check out our full list of GTA alternatives for kids for more recommendations.

title: How To Unlock The Alien Questline in GTA 6
summary: Aliens are real (In Grand Theft Auto VI) and we’re going to show you exactly how to kick off and complete the secret UFO missions in Rockstar’s open world game.
